**Bottom line:** Refex's FY2025-26 picture is dominated by a working-capital squeeze: trade receivables plus contract assets in Ash & Coal Handling reached Rs.1,41,320.13 lakhs (58.34% of total assets), receivables grew while cash fell, and the current ratio declined on higher current liabilities [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.266][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.259][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.327]. These red flags are partly offset by a reaffirmed investment-grade-style rating (Acuité A-: Stable long-term / A2+: short-term, letter dated January 08, 2026), unmodified audit opinions, a DSCR that improved on higher earnings, and no material going-concern doubt flagged [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.76][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.121][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.181][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.264][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.195]. The rating is supported by earnings growth, not by balance-sheet strength, so receivable quality is the key swing factor.

## Liquidity and working-capital position
- Liquidity is monitored on monthly and yearly projections; stated sources are cash and cash equivalents, cash from operations, term loans from banks and share capital, with short-term needs mainly sundry creditors, expense payable, employee dues, loan repayment and retentions/deposits [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.247][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.330].
- The current ratio declined on account of an increase in current liabilities [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.259].
- Cash and cash equivalents (amortized cost) fell to Rs.18,370.81 lakhs at 31 March 2026 from Rs.28,149.24 lakhs at 31 March 2025, while bank balances other than cash and cash equivalents rose to Rs.20,963.82 lakhs from Rs.7,055.30 lakhs [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.327][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.329].
- Other current financial liabilities were Rs.21,006.68 lakhs and short-term borrowings Rs.13,328.63 lakhs at 31 March 2026, against trade payables of Rs.46,428.40 lakhs, up from Rs.17,172.56 lakhs a year earlier [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.327].
- The auditor states no material uncertainty exists as of the audit report date over the Company meeting liabilities falling due within one year, while expressly disclaiming any assurance on future viability [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.195].

## Leverage and debt profile
- Long-term borrowings fell to Rs.2,882.09 lakhs at 31 March 2026 from Rs.9,184.06 lakhs; short-term borrowings rose to Rs.13,328.63 lakhs from Rs.7,983.54 lakhs; lease liability was Rs.6,293.70 lakhs [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.327].
- Debt-equity decreased due to an increase in shareholders' equity, and the debt-service coverage ratio increased due to higher current earnings [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.259].
- The Company has sanctioned working-capital limits exceeding Rs.5 crore from banks on security of current assets; monthly statements filed with banks agree with the books, as do the group's quarterly current-asset returns [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.192][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.262].
- The Company has not been declared a wilful defaulter by any bank, financial institution or government authority [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.345].
- Interest-bearing financial instruments are described as all fixed-rate borrowings, so the Company states it assumes no interest-rate-increase risk [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.249].

## Receivables, inventory and cash-conversion quality
- Trade receivables and contract assets in the Ash and Coal Handling segment were Rs.1,41,320.13 lakhs at 31 March 2026, about 58.34% of total assets (consolidated; the standalone note gives Rs.1,41,320.12 lakhs) [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.266][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.183].
- Contract-asset recognition depends on management judgement in measuring ash disposed and obtaining customer certification; unbilled revenue uses a unit of measure different from the Daily Progress Report, and DPRs are prepared by management [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.266][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.183].
- Trade receivables rose to Rs.88,625 lakhs at 31 March 2026 from Rs.67,677 lakhs at 31 March 2025; receivables are typically unsecured and the Company states it is not exposed to concentration of credit risk to any single customer [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.246][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.329].
- Trade receivable turnover declined due to higher debtor receivable days, trade payable turnover declined due to lower creditor payable days, and net capital turnover declined because working capital rose faster than turnover [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.259].
- The FY2025 ageing schedule shows undisputed trade receivables considered good of Rs.67,758.53 lakhs, less allowance for credit loss of Rs.81.08 lakhs, for a net Rs.67,677.46 lakhs [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.303].
- ECL is measured under the Ind AS 109 simplified approach; management assesses recoverability case-by-case considering ageing, customer creditworthiness, disputes, subsequent receipts, collateral and credit enhancements, and receivables judged fully recoverable are not provided for [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.246][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.330][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.247].
- Inventory was physically verified by management with no discrepancies of 10% or more in aggregate for any class [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.192].

## Related-party transactions, loans/guarantees and contingent liabilities
- Transactions with Venwind Refex Power Limited (subsidiary) during FY2025-26 included loans and advances, interest income on loans and OCDs, issuance of corporate guarantees, investments and lease/rental income; recorded values include investments of Rs.10,293.14 lakhs and OCDs of Rs.5,203 lakhs [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.81].
- The Company made investments in, and provided guarantees/securities and loans or advances to companies and other parties; terms were stated not prejudicial to the Company's interest [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.192].
- Related-party transactions in FY2025-26 are stated to be on an arm's length basis and in the ordinary course of business under Section 188(1), with no material transaction conflicting with the Company's interests [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.70][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.121].
- Assessment of contingent liabilities for direct and indirect tax litigations and third-party claims not acknowledged as debt is a Key Audit Matter due to the high judgement and uncertainty involved (Note 34 standalone, Note 38 consolidated) [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.184][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.267].

## Auditor opinion, key audit matters and internal-control findings
- The statutory auditor is A B C D & Co. LLP; the internal auditor is M/s Sudarsan & Co. [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.58].
- Both the standalone and consolidated Ind AS financial statements received unmodified true-and-fair-view opinions as at 31 March 2026 [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.181][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.264].
- Key Audit Matters are trade receivables and contract assets in the Coal and Ash Handling segment (recognition, recoverability and ECL), and assessment of contingent liabilities [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.266][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.183][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.184][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.267].
- The Audit Committee noted, as of 31 March 2026, the Company's internal financial controls position; the statutory auditors issued an attestation report on internal control over financial reporting under Section 143 of the Companies Act, 2013 [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.58]. No material weakness finding is disclosed in the evidence.

## Business segment and customer concentration / going-concern and litigation risks
- Revenue mix: Ash & Coal handling 83% of turnover, Windpower 9.85%, Refex mobility 4.13% [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.131]. Ash & Coal Handling segment revenue was Rs.2,013 crore; Wind Energy Rs.238 crore; Mobility rose 164% from Rs.38 crore to Rs.100 crore [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.57].
- Concentration in thermal power off-takers (NTPC, state discoms) creates counterparty and policy risk; mitigation cited is 40+ thermal plant clients across 14+ states [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.135].
- Operations comprise Coal & Ash Handling, Wind Energy Solutions (via Venwind Refex Power Limited) and Premium Corporate Mobility (via Refex Green Mobility Limited) [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.54].
- The Board approved discontinuation of the Power Trading segment on 12 August 2025 and of the Refrigerant Gases segment on 21 January 2026 (about 2.50% of total revenue); both qualify as discontinued operations under Ind AS 105 [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.203][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.261][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.344].
- No significant or material order by regulators, courts or tribunals affects going-concern status or future operations other than matters in Note 34 [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.72].
- Litigation: pending criminal, tax, statutory/regulatory and other material proceedings; adverse outcomes could affect profitability, reputation and financial condition [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.238][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.320]. Specific suits include claims of Rs.29,45,233 against Shekhar Refrigeration, Rs.4,11,635 against Refrigeration Spare Centre, Rs.5,12,549 against Sikelan Chemicals and Rs.36,95,272 against Atmos Industries [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.322].

## Credit rating held and rationale
- Acuité Ratings & Research Limited, by letter dated January 08, 2026, reaffirmed the ratings on the Company's bank loan facilities: long-term bank facilities (term loans) at ACUITE A-: Stable and short-term bank facilities (cash credit) at ACUITE A2+, both reaffirmed [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.76][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.121].
- The evidence does not disclose the rating agency's rationale or rating sensitivity factors.

## Revenue mix, profitability and cash-flow trends
- Standalone turnover was Rs.2,075 crore vs Rs.2,430 crore in the prior year, the decline attributed to discontinuation of the low-margin Power Trading and Refrigerant businesses; PBT rose 38.17% to Rs.333 crore (from Rs.241 crore) and PAT rose 30% to Rs.246 crore (from Rs.189 crore) [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.55].
- Net profit ratio increased due to higher revenue in a higher-margin segment [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.259].
- Cash flow statement: net profit before tax (continuing and discontinuing operations) was Rs.27,747.11 lakhs for FY2025-26 vs Rs.19,991.35 lakhs for FY2024-25 [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.277].
- Discontinued operations recorded revenue of Rs.13,490.18 lakhs, total expenses of Rs.18,897.00 lakhs, pre-tax loss of Rs.5,295.93 lakhs and post-tax loss of Rs.3,866.18 lakhs for the year ended 31 March 2026 [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.345].

## Not addressed in the evidence
- The evidence provides no numeric interest-coverage ratio, no explicit current-ratio value, and no quantified contingent-liability or guarantee amounts, and no rating rationale from Acuité.

chunks.section: Expected Credit Loss (ECL) on Trade Receivables:
chunks.text: The Company applies the simplified approach prescribed under Ind AS 109 for recognition of Expected Credit Loss (""ECL"") on trade receivables and contract assets. The Company assesses impairment of trade receivables at each reporting date based on management's estimate of the recoverability of the outstanding balances. The ECL allowance is determined on a case- to-case basis after considering all relevant facts and circumstances available as at the reporting date.

of Financial statements While evaluating the recoverability of receivables, management considers factors including, but not limited to: • Ageing of receivables and historical payment trends; • Creditworthiness and financial position of the customer; • Past collection experience with the customer; • Existence of disputes, claims, litigations or contractual issues; • Subsequent receipts after the reporting date; • Industry and economic conditions impacting the customer; • Availability of collateral, security deposits, bank guarantees or other credit enhancements; and • Any other information indicating a significant increase in credit risk or impairment. Receivables assessed as fully recoverable are not provided for. Specific provisions are created against receivables where, based on management's assessment, there exists an expectation of credit loss. The amount of provision represents management's best estimate of the expected shortfall in contractual cash flows considering all reasonable and supportable information available at the reporting date. The Company reviews the adequacy of the impairment allowance at each reporting date and adjusts the provision based on changes in facts, circumstances and expectations of recovery. Actual credit losses may differ from these estimates. Receivables considered irrecoverable are written off upon completion of the Company's internal recovery assessment and approval process. chunks.text: Your Company has adopted a “Policy on Related Party Transactions”, in accordance with the provisions of the Act and Regulation 23 of the Listing Regulations, inter-alia, providing a framework for governance and reporting of Related Party Transactions including material transactions and threshold limits for determining materiality. The said Policy is also available on the website of the Company at the web-link: https://refex.co.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/RIL_RPT_Policy_Jan26.pdf All related party transactions that were entered into during the financial year ended on March 31, 2026 were on an arm’s length basis and in the ordinary course of business under Section 188(1) of the Act and the Listing Regulations. Details of the transactions with related parties are provided in note no. 40 of the accompanying financial statements, in compliance with the provision of Section 134(3)(h) of the Act. All related party transactions and subsequent material modifications, if any, are placed before the Audit Committee for review and approval. **Bottom line:** The evidence does not quantify how much of Refex Industries' balance sheet is tied up in group entities, nor does it provide the full balance-sheet line items or a Note 40 related-party balance schedule needed to compute it. What the evidence does show is a sharp increase in loans/advances/guarantees to subsidiaries on the standalone books — aggregate amounts granted rose to ₹46,310.00 lakh and balances outstanding to ₹50,937.45 lakh (from ₹3,792.42 lakh and ₹8,916.42 lakh respectively) — alongside an inter-corporate deposit of ₹4,500.00 lakh to subsidiaries and corporate guarantees issued to VRPL. No evidence quantifies off-balance-sheet commitments or contingent liabilities involving group entities, so the year-on-year change on that aspect cannot be computed.

## Standalone and consolidated balance sheet figures (investments, loans/advances to group entities)
- Standalone loans and advances to subsidiaries (measured at amortised cost) include inter-corporate deposits of ₹4,500.00 lakh [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.224]; the same ₹4,500.00 lakh inter-corporate deposit appears in other current financial assets, alongside short-term deposits of ₹2,955.72 lakh [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.304].
- Standalone auditor's report (Section 186-type disclosure) shows aggregate amounts granted/provided during the year: Subsidiaries ₹46,310.00 lakh (PY ₹3,792.42 lakh); balance outstanding at balance sheet date: Subsidiaries ₹50,937.45 lakh (PY ₹8,916.42 lakh); Other than subsidiaries: nil granted, ₹3,748.00 lakh outstanding at balance sheet date (PY nil); Holding company, associates and fellow subsidiaries: nil in both years [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.192].
- The transaction table referred to in the standalone CARO disclosure (loans, guarantees and security to subsidiaries and associates) is not reproduced with figures in the evidence beyond the above [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.192].
- No consolidated balance-sheet figures for investments in or loans/advances to group entities are given in the evidence (consolidated statements eliminate intra-group balances) [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.284].
- Section 186 particulars of loans, guarantees or investments are stated to be in Note 43 to the standalone financial statements, which is not reproduced in the evidence [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.73].

## Related party transactions and balances with group entities
- All related party transactions in FY2025-26 are stated to be on an arm's-length basis and in the ordinary course of business under Section 188(1) of the Act and the Listing Regulations; details are in Note 40 of the financial statements [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.70].
- There are no material significant related party transactions that may conflict with the Company's interest; members are referred to Note 40 [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.121].
- Loans/advances to firms/companies in which directors are interested: none during FY ended March 31, 2026, except loans extended to the subsidiary and wholly-owned subsidiaries, details in Note 40 [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.127].
- Transactions with VRPL during FY2025-26 included loans and advances, interest income on loans and Optionally Convertible Debentures (OCDs), issuance of corporate guarantees, investments, and lease/rental income [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.81].
- Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report concentration metrics: share of RPTs in purchases 0.07% (PY) / NA (current); sales to related parties 0.08% (current) vs 0.35% (PY); loans & advances given to related parties as % of total loans & advances 0% (current) vs 100% (PY); investments in related parties as % of total investments 0% (current) vs 100% (PY) [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.145].
- Note 40, which contains the actual related party balances and transaction amounts, is not reproduced in the evidence [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.70][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.121].

## Off-balance-sheet commitments and contingent liabilities involving group entities
- Contingent liabilities are disclosed for possible obligations from past events; show cause notices are not treated as contingent liabilities unless converted into demand (accounting policy) [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.211][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.292].
- Contingent liabilities relating to direct and indirect tax litigations and claims by other parties are a Key Audit Matter; the Group's assessment is disclosed in Note 38 (consolidated) and the Company's in Note 34 (standalone) — amounts and whether any involve group entities are not given in the evidence [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.267][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.184].
- Corporate guarantees were issued to VRPL during FY2025-26 as part of the transactions with that subsidiary [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.81]; the guarantee amount is not quantified in the evidence.
- The standalone auditor reports the Company has not taken funds from any entity or person to meet the obligations of its subsidiaries, associates or joint ventures (Clause 3(ix)(f) not applicable) [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.194].
- No other off-balance-sheet commitments involving group entities are quantified in the evidence [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.75].

## Year-on-year change versus prior year
- Loans/advances granted to subsidiaries: ₹46,310.00 lakh in FY2025-26 vs ₹3,792.42 lakh in FY2024-25 [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.192].
- Balances outstanding with subsidiaries at balance sheet date: ₹50,937.45 lakh vs ₹8,916.42 lakh prior year; other parties ₹3,748.00 lakh vs nil [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.192].
- Related-party share of loans & advances moved from 100% in FY2024-25 to 0% in FY2025-26, and of investments from 100% to 0% [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.145].
- For contingent liabilities and guarantees involving group entities, the evidence does not provide comparative prior-year amounts, so the change cannot be quantified [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.267][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.184][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.81].

## Composition of the group/subsidiaries and their business segments
- Holding company: Refex Holding Private Limited (formerly Sherisha Technologies Private Limited) holds 55.85% [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.133][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.64].
- Subsidiaries as at March 31, 2026: Refex Green Mobility Limited (RGML) 100% wholly-owned; Refex Mobility Limited (RML) 100% wholly-owned (incorporated September 12, 2025); Refex EV Fleet Services Private Limited (formerly O3 Mobility) 100% step-down; Venwind Refex Power Limited (VRPL) 77.39%; Venwind Refex Power Services Limited 77.39% step-down; Refex Engineering Products Private Limited 77.39% step-down; Venwind Refex Projects Limited 77.39% step-down [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.133].
- REPPL was acquired from Refex Holding Private Limited on December 05, 2025 by secondary transfer; Venwind Refex Projects Limited was incorporated November 25, 2025; post-year-end the Company holds 73.28% indirectly [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.84].
- Business segments: Coal & Ash Handling (largest vertical); Wind Energy Solutions through VRPL; Premium Corporate Mobility through RGML [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.54]; main activity turnover split: ash & coal handling 83%, windpower (wind turbine trading and manufacturing) 9.85%, Refex mobility 4.13% [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.131].
- Discontinued segments: Power Trading and Refrigerant Gases (Board approvals August 12, 2025 and January 21, 2026) [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.264]; Green mobility is listed among discontinued operations in the standalone note [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.281].
- A Composite Scheme of Amalgamation and Arrangement among RGML, Refex Industries Limited and others was approved by the Board on September 22, 2025 [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.264].

Contingent liabilities are disclosed when there is a possible obligation arising from past events, the existence of which will be confirmed only by the occurrence or non-occurrence of one or more uncertain future events not wholly within the control of the Company or a present obligation that arises from past events where it is either not probable that an outflow of resources will be required to settle or a reliable estimate of the amount cannot be made, is termed as a contingent liability. Show cause notices are not considered as Contingent Liabilities unless converted into demand. j.Leases The Company, as a lessee, recognises a right-of-use asset and a lease liability for its leasing arrangements, if the contract conveys the right to control the use of an identified asset. The contract conveys the right to control the use of an identified asset, if it involves the use of an identified asset and the Company has substantially all of the economic benefits from use of the asset and has the right to direct the use of the identified asset. The cost of the right-of-use asset shall comprise of the amount of the initial measurement of the lease liability adjusted for any lease payments made at or before the commencement date plus any initial direct costs incurred. The right-of-use assets is subsequently measured at cost less any accumulated depreciation, accumulated impairment losses, if any and adjusted for any remeasurement of the lease liability. The right-of-use assets are depreciated using the straight-line method from the commencement date over the shorter of lease term or useful life of the right-of-use asset. The Company measures the lease liability at the present value of the lease payments that are not paid at the commencement date of the lease.

The swing is an arithmetic artefact, not a change in fundamentals. FY2024-25's Debt Service Coverage Ratio of 2.24 was depressed (from 327.62 in FY2023-24) by a one-time interest payment to HSIIDC that pushed finance cost to Rs. 237.41 lakhs on flat earnings [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2025 p.105][Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2025 p.37][Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2025 p.36]; with that cost gone in FY2025-26 (finance cost Rs. 1.41 lakhs), the same earnings base produced a DSCR of 211.18 [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.110][Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.38][Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.107]. Underlying debt service capacity deteriorated modestly: EBIT fell (PBT Rs. 318.69 lakhs vs Rs. 307.78 lakhs, but profitability came from lower finance cost and other income, and ROCE dropped from 13.03% to 7.18%), debt doubled and net debt rose from Rs. 137.91 to Rs. 327.82 lakhs [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.110][Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.37][Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.89][Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.39].

## Debt-service / coverage and leverage ratios reported in each year
- FY2024-25: DSCR 2.24x (vs 327.62x in FY2023-24, -99.32%), Debt-Equity 0.04x (vs 0.05x), Interest Coverage (EBIT/Interest) 2.30x (vs 345.49x) [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2025 p.105][Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2025 p.37].
- FY2025-26: DSCR 211.18x (vs 2.24x, +9,322.11%), Interest Coverage 227.02x (vs 2.30x, +9,785.75%), Debt-Equity 0.08x (vs 0.04x, +111.53%) [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.110][Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.38].
- FY2025-26 ROCE 7.18% vs 13.03% (-44.88%) and EBITDA margin 2.53% vs 3.78% (-33.07%) [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.39].

## Profitability trend driving the numerator of coverage ratios
- FY2024-25: profit before finance cost Rs. 545.20 lakhs, finance cost Rs. 237.41 lakhs, PBT Rs. 307.78 lakhs, PAT Rs. 236.96 lakhs; prior year finance cost was only Rs. 0.93 lakhs [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2025 p.36][Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2025 p.83].
- FY2025-26: profit before finance cost Rs. 320.10 lakhs, finance cost Rs. 1.41 lakhs, PBT Rs. 318.69 lakhs, PAT Rs. 239.97 lakhs [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.37][Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.89].
- Revenue fell from Rs. 16,025.02 lakhs to Rs. 14,897.55 lakhs while PBT rose only marginally (Rs. 239.97 lakhs per the Board's narrative vs Rs. 236.96 lakhs prior year, described as 'marginal growth') [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.89][Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.7].
- Net profit ratio 1.61% vs 1.48% in FY2025-26, but ROCE and EBITDA margin fell on 'lower earning (before interest)' [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.39].

## Borrowings and capital structure changes between years
- Total borrowings: Rs. 352.11 lakhs at 31.03.2026 vs Rs. 159.64 lakhs at 31.03.2025; cash and cash equivalents including deposits Rs. 24.29 vs Rs. 21.73 lakhs; adjusted net debt Rs. 327.82 vs Rs. 137.91 lakhs [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.110].
- Total equity Rs. 4,397.00 vs Rs. 4,216.96 lakhs [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.110].
- FY2024-25 borrowings were Rs. 159.64 lakhs vs Rs. 204.21 lakhs at 31.03.2024, with the D/E fall attributed to 'improvement in equity' [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2025 p.105][Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2025 p.103].
- FY2025-26 D/E rise attributed to 'increase in debts of the company' [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.38].
- Cash flow statement: proceeds from new borrowings (Overdraft Limit) Rs. 192.47 lakhs in FY2025-26 vs Rs. (44.57) lakhs in FY2024-25; dividend paid Rs. 73.27 lakhs vs nil [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.91].

## Cash flow and liquidity position affecting ability to service debt
- Operating cash flow turned negative in FY2025-26: net cash used in operating activities Rs. (115.84) lakhs vs Rs. 569.06 lakhs generated in FY2024-25 [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.91].
- Cash generated from operations Rs. (24.51) lakhs vs Rs. 673.76 lakhs; trade receivables absorbed Rs. (674.56) lakhs vs a release of Rs. 624.42 lakhs [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.91].
- Closing cash and cash equivalents Rs. 10.85 lakhs vs Rs. 8.56 lakhs [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.91].
- Current ratio 4.49x vs 4.73x (-5.13%) [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.110][Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.38].
- All current financial liabilities (borrowings Rs. 352.11, trade payables Rs. 107.90, other financial liabilities Rs. 151.62 lakhs) are contractually due in less than one year [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.109].
- No default in payment of interest or repayment of loans to financial lenders in either year [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2025 p.8][Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.10][Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2025 p.77][Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.83]; auditor states no material uncertainty about meeting liabilities falling due within one year [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.85].
- Long-term credit rating 'ACUITE BBB' and short-term 'ACUITE A3+' reaffirmed in FY2025-26 with 'Stable' outlook [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.68].

## Explanations/disclosures of ratio movements and one-off items
- FY2024-25: DSCR and interest coverage falls expressly attributed to 'one-time payment of interest cost to HSIIDC' [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2025 p.105][Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2025 p.37].
- FY2025-26: DSCR and interest coverage rises attributed to 'reduction in Interest Cost' / 'lower finance cost' [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.110][Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.38].
- FY2024-25 Board commentary attributes the profit decline 'primarily to an increase in finance costs' [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2025 p.6].
- Definitions: Debt Service = Finance cost + Interest on leases + Principal Repayment; Earning Available for Debt Service = PAT + D&A + finance cost excluding lease interest + other non-cash adjustments [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2025 p.105].

## Assessment of whether underlying debt-servicing ability improved or weakened
- Headline DSCR improvement from 2.24x to 211.18x is driven by the absence of the one-off HSIIDC interest (finance cost Rs. 1.41 vs Rs. 237.41 lakhs), not by earnings growth [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.37][Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2025 p.36][Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.107].
- Earnings before interest fell (profit before finance cost Rs. 320.10 vs Rs. 545.20 lakhs) and ROCE declined to 7.18% from 13.03% [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.37][Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.39].
- Leverage rose (D/E 0.08x vs 0.04x; adjusted net debt Rs. 327.82 vs Rs. 137.91 lakhs) and operating cash flow turned negative, so underlying debt-servicing ability weakened despite the reported ratio jump [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.110][Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.91].
- Liquidity explanation for the swing in the prior year is the inverse one-off: FY2024-25 DSCR of 2.24x understates normalised coverage because an exceptional interest outflow inflated the denominator [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2025 p.105][Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2025 p.37].
- The evidence does not disclose the size or period of the HSIIDC one-time interest payment, nor a DSCR normalised for it.

chunks.section: REVIEW OF FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE AND STATE OF COMPANY’S AFFAIRS
chunks.text: During the financial year under review, the Company recorded revenue from operations of Rs. 14,897.55 Lakhs as compared to Rs. 16,025.02 Lakhs in the previous financial year. The decline in revenue during the year was primarily attributable to relatively challenging market conditions prevailing in the steel industry, including increased competition, volatility in raw material and steel prices, pressure on margins, and subdued demand from certain end-user sectors. The industry also witnessed fluctuations in domestic and global market dynamics, which impacted overall sales volumes during the year. In addition, the ongoing conflict in Iran and the Middle East caused problems in global energy supply, higher freight and shipping costs, and changes in international raw material prices during the year. This also disturbed the movement of steel and raw materials across global markets, adding further uncertainty to the industry. Although the Company mainly operates in the domestic market, these global issues still had an effect on overall demand within the domestic steel industry, which impacted sales and turnover during the year. Despite these challenges, the Company continued to focus on maintaining customer relationships, operational efficiency and market presence. Further, the Company reported profit before tax of Rs. 239.97 Lakhs for the financial year ended March 31, 2026, as against Rs. 236.96 Lakhs in the previous year, reflecting a marginal growth in profitability. The improvement in profit was supported by effective cost optimization measures, improved operational efficiencies, and focused resource management initiatives undertaken by the Company.

chunks.section: REVIEW OF PERFORMANCE AND STATE OF COMPANY’S AFFAIRS
chunks.text: The Company reported revenue from operations of ₹16,025.02 lakhs as compared to ₹16,841.44 lakhs in the previous financial year. This decline reflects the broader challenges faced by the steel industry during the year, including intensified competition, fluctuations in global steel prices, and a slowdown in demand across key domestic and international markets. Further, the Company reported a net profit of ₹236.96 lakhs for the financial year ended March 31, 2025, as against ₹249.83 lakhs in the previous financial year, reflecting a marginal decline. The decrease in profitability was primarily attributable to an increase in finance costs, which exerted downward pressure on the bottom line. Looking forward, the Company is actively exploring strategic initiatives aimed at enhancing financial performance. Key focus areas include improving working capital efficiency, optimizing cost structures, and implementing targeted operational efficiencies. These measures are expected to support profitability and strengthen the Company’s financial resilience in the coming years. The management remains cautiously optimistic about the future prospects and is committed to navigating through these challenging times with resilience and adaptability.

answer:
**Bottom line:** Bhadora Industries' FY2024-25 growth was financed mainly by a sharp increase in short-term bank borrowings (up Rs. 653.39 lakhs) and long-term borrowings (up Rs. 366.22 lakhs), supplemented by internal accruals, while the Rs. 5,562.00 lakhs IPO was allotted but not received during the year per the auditor's CARO statement. This debt-funded growth has flowed into receivables: trade receivables rose from Rs. 1,219.65 lakhs to Rs. 2,177.41 lakhs, receivable turnover collapsed 83.26% to 1.62, and the current ratio is thin at 1.59, which is the key lender concern.

## How growth is being financed
- Cash flow from financing activities in FY2024-25 shows long-term borrowings of Rs. 366.22 lakhs and proceeds from short-term borrowings of Rs. 653.39 lakhs, against finance cost paid of Rs. 277.77 lakhs [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.72].
- Net cash from operating activities was Rs. 351.68 lakhs post-working-capital, versus Rs. 271.58 lakhs in the prior year [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.72].
- Net cash used in investing activities was Rs. 845.17 lakhs, mainly acquisition of fixed assets of Rs. 729.95 lakhs, versus Rs. 136.10 lakhs in FY2023-24 [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.72].
- The auditor's CARO annexure states the company did not raise any money by way of initial public offer or further public offer (including debt instruments) during the year, and made no preferential allotment or private placement [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.65].
- Short-term borrowings rose from Rs. 829.89 lakhs to Rs. 1,483.29 lakhs, and long-term borrowings from Rs. 17.49 lakhs to Rs. 483.35 lakhs, between 31.03.2024 and 31.03.2025 [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.70].
- Working capital demand loan is availed from Yes Bank for working capital at an ROI of 10.25% [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.75].
- The company has sanctioned working capital limits from banks secured by hypothecation of stock and assignment of debtors [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.63][Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.64].
- The company has not accepted any deposits within the meaning of sections 73 to 76 of the Act [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.65].
- The company transferred Rs. 300 lakhs to General Reserve for FY ended 31st March 2025 [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.21].

## Receivables quality and ageing
- Trade receivables were Rs. 2,177.41 lakhs as at 31.03.2025 versus Rs. 1,219.65 lakhs as at 31.03.2024 [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.76][Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.70].
- Ageing as at March 31, 2025 (undisputed): Rs. 1,997.61 lakhs less than 6 months, Rs. 96.26 lakhs 6 months-1 year, Rs. 38.63 lakhs 1-2 years, Rs. 8.79 lakhs 2-3 years; no disputed receivables [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.76].
- Ageing as at March 31, 2024 (undisputed): Rs. 953.51 lakhs less than 6 months, Rs. 132.58 lakhs 6 months-1 year, Rs. 123.82 lakhs 1-2 years, Rs. 8.79 lakhs 2-3 years; no disputed receivables [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.76].
- Trade receivable turnover ratio fell to 1.62 from 9.68, a decline of 83.26%, attributed to an increase in trade receivables [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.41].
- Debtors as per books versus statements submitted to the bank showed variations, e.g. Rs. 1,537.93 vs Rs. 1,533.59, Rs. 1,924.00 vs Rs. 2,137.73, Rs. 1,535.23 vs Rs. 1,533.59, Rs. 1,923.97 vs Rs. 2,180.59, with a variance of Rs. 42.86 attributed to an auditor change of one creditor to the debtors list [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.81].
- The company has filed quarterly returns/statements with banks on the security of current assets which are in agreement with the books other than material differences set out [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.63]; quarterly working capital return figures versus sanctioned/offered limits include June 30: 2,184.97 vs 2,428.3 (difference 243.36), September: 2,241.58 vs 2,549.1 (307.58), December: 3,175.63 vs 3,175.6 (-0.03), March: 3,053.54 vs 3,162.0 (108.67) [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.64].

## Working capital position and cycle
- Inventories were Rs. 981.42 lakhs as at 31.03.2025 (raw material Rs. 266.24 lakhs, finished goods Rs. 483.46 lakhs, WIP Rs. 231.71 lakhs) versus Rs. 829.20 lakhs as at 31.03.2024 [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.76].
- Inventory turnover improved to 12.16 from 9.13, a 33.21% increase, attributed to improved inventory management and faster movement of stock [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.41].
- Trade payables were Rs. 416.41 lakhs as at 31.03.2025 (MSME Rs. 384.85 lakhs; others Rs. 31.56 lakhs) versus Rs. 466.98 lakhs as at 31.03.2024 (MSME Rs. 312.55 lakhs; others Rs. 154.44 lakhs) [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.75].
- Trade payable turnover rose to 19.21 from 14.80, a 29.73% increase, indicating quicker settlement of dues or reduced credit period availed [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.41][Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.75].
- Cash flow working capital changes in FY2024-25 include inventories (152.22), trade receivables (957.75), short-term loans and advances (24.80), other current assets 0.19, trade payables (50.57), other current liabilities 58.32 [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.72].
- Trade receivables turnover ratio decline is attributed to increase in trade receivables, and net capital turnover ratio also declined [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.81].

## Liquidity and leverage ratios
- Current ratio: 1.59 as at 30.03.25 versus 1.55 as at 31.03.24 (change 2.58%, not significant) [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.81][Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.41].
- Debt-equity ratio: 0.94 as at 30.03.25 versus 0.89 as at 31.03.24 (change 5.62%, not significant) [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.81][Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.41].
- Debt service coverage ratio: 5.06 [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.81].
- Return on equity: 0.49 versus 0.47 [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.81].
- Return on capital employed: 0.40 versus 0.42, a 4.76% decline (not significant) [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.81][Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.42].
- Return on net worth: 64.39 versus 61.35 [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.42].
- Net profit margin: 0.09 versus 0.06, a 50.00% increase attributed to better profitability, cost control and improved sales margins [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.41][Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.42].
- The auditor states, based on financial ratios, ageing and expected dates of realisation of financial assets and payment of financial liabilities, that no material uncertainty exists as on the date of the audit report and the company is capable of meeting its liabilities existing at the balance sheet date as and when they fall due within one year [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.66].
- The company has not defaulted in repayment of loans or borrowings to a financial institution, bank, Government or dues to debenture holders [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.65].
- Cash and cash equivalents were Rs. 276.50 lakhs as at 31.03.2025 versus Rs. 28.14 lakhs as at 31.03.2024 [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.72][Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.76].

## Revenue and profitability growth
- Total income for FY2024-25 was INR 110,69,33,000 (Rs. 11,069.33 lakhs) versus INR 83,27,48,000 (Rs. 8,327.48 lakhs) in FY2023-24 [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.20].
- Turnover for the reporting period was INR 11,011.18 lakhs [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.19][Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.5].
- Profit after tax for FY2024-25 was INR 10,14,93,000 (Rs. 1,014.93 lakhs) versus INR 5,01,79,000 (Rs. 501.79 lakhs) in FY2023-24 [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.20][Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.5].
- Net profit before tax and depreciation was Rs. 1,385.51 lakhs versus Rs. 501.79 lakhs in the previous year [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.41]; profit before tax per the cash flow statement was Rs. 1,385.51 lakhs versus Rs. 676.65 lakhs [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.72].
- Net cash flow from operating activities was Rs. 351.68 lakhs versus Rs. 271.58 lakhs in the prior year [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.72].
- The company has not incurred any cash losses in the financial year or the immediately preceding financial year [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.66].

## SME platform listing and IPO details
- The company received NSE in-principle approval for its proposed IPO through the book building process on the NSE Emerge platform, per letter dated May 09, 2025 [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.34][Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.47][Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.46].
- The IPO aggregated to INR 5,562.00 lakhs (Issue Size), comprising 54,00,000 equity shares at INR 103 per share (face value Rs. 10 and premium of Rs. 93) [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.21].
- Total capital of Rs. 5,562.00 lakhs, consisting of 54,00,000 equity shares of face value Rs. 10 each, has been listed and authorised for trading on the NSE Emerge SME platform with effect from August 11, 2025 [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.34][Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.47].
- The equity shares were listed on NSE SME on Monday, August 11, 2025 [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.21][Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.5][Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.32].
- A bonus issue of 1,15,50,000 equity shares of Rs. 10 each was issued and allotted, dated 31/12/2024 [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.21].
- The company's status was converted into a public limited company, with the name changed from Bhadora Industries Private Limited to Bhadora Industries Limited, and a fresh Certificate of Incorporation dated August 07, 2024 issued by the Registrar of Companies, Gwalior, CPC [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.34].
- As an NSE Emerge-listed company, it is exempt from compulsory adoption of IND-AS under Rule 4(1) of the Companies (Indian Accounting Standards) Rules, 2015 [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.23].
- The company claims exemption under Regulation 15(2) of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 from corporate governance provisions in regulations 17 to 27, clauses (b) to (i) and (t) of sub-regulation (2) of regulation 46, and paras C, D and E of Schedule V [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.36].

## Not addressed in the evidence
- The evidence does not state the amount of IPO proceeds actually received by the company or their application, beyond the CARO statement that no IPO money was raised during the year [Bhadora Industries_Annual Report p.65].

chunks.section: STATE OF AFFAIRS OF THE COMPANY
chunks.text: The Company is mainly engaged in the business of Cable Manufacturing. During the year under review, the Company has put all its efforts in serving required products to all its customers on time. The turnover of the Company during the reporting period amounted to INR 11,011.18 Lakhs. The directors are thankful to all its suppliers, distributors for on time delivery of the products. The Directors assure the stakeholders of the Company to continue their efforts and enhance the overall performance of the Company in the coming financial years. The Directors express their gratitude towards the stakeholders for all the support that the Company has received

GREETINGS!! It gives me immense pleasure to welcome you all to the 12th Annual General Meeting of Bhadora Industries Limited (Vidhut Cables). On behalf of the Board of Directors, I extend my heartfelt gratitude for your continued support, trust, and encouragement that has enabled our Company to progress with strength and resilience. I am delighted to share with you the highlights of our Company’s performance for the financial year 2024–25. Despite a highly competitive and challenging environment, Bhadora Industries Limited achieved a revenue of₹11,011.18 lakhs, reflecting the strength of our business model and the commitment of our people. Further, we recorded a net profit of ₹1,014.93 lakhs, a testimony to our operational efficiency, disciplined cost management, and value creation for our stakeholders. This year also marks a significant milestone in the journey of Bhadora Industries Limited on August 11, 2025, our Company was successfully listed on the Small and Medium Enterprises (SME) Exchange. This achievement is not just a recognition of our consistent performance, but also a gateway to new opportunities, enhanced visibility, and greater access to capital markets. I take this moment to thank all our shareholders, employees, bankers, advisors, and well-wishers who played a vital role in making this possible.

**Bottom line:** On the evidence available, Inox Wind shows by far the largest related-party dependence relative to size — loans/advances to related parties were 64.74% of total loans and advances in FY2025-26, sales to related parties 12.88% of total sales, ICDs of ₹2,11,663.40 lakh repayable on demand to related parties, and it is openly availing funding from group entity Inox Clean Energy Limited and promoter director Shri Devansh Jain [Inox Wind_Annual Report FY 2026 p.153][Inox Wind_Annual Report FY 2026 p.187][Inox Wind_Annual Report FY 2026 p.68][Inox Wind_Annual Report FY 2026 p.88]. Refex shows related-party sales at only 0.08% of total sales but carries group exposure through loans to subsidiaries and corporate guarantees for Venwind Refex Power Limited [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.145][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.81]. Metal Coatings and GRM Overseas disclose negligible or mostly trade-nature related-party exposure, with GRM's related-party loans being borrowings *from* related parties rather than lending to them [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.140][Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2025 p.29][Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.31][GRM Overseas_Annual Report FY 2025 p.213][GRM Overseas_Annual Report FY 2025 p.261].

## Refex Industries — related-party loan, guarantee, sales and receivable balances
- Share of related-party transactions in FY2025-26: purchases with related parties NA; sales to related parties 0.08% of total sales (FY2024-25: 0.35%); loans & advances given to related parties 0% of total loans & advances (FY2024-25: 100%); investments in related parties 0% of total investments (FY2024-25: 100%) [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.145].
- Transactions with subsidiary Venwind Refex Power Limited in FY2025-26 included loans and advances, interest income on loans and OCDs, issuance of corporate guarantees, investments and lease/rental income [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.81]; recorded amounts for that entity include rental income net of loans/advances given and repayment received, investments of 10,293.14, OCD 5,203, reimbursement expenses and interest received [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.81].
- Loans and advances to subsidiaries measured at amortized cost include 8,277.50 to Refex Green Mobility Limited [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.225]; loans/advances to Venwind Refex Power Limited carry interest at 9% per annum [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.224].
- A material related party transaction resolution with Venwind Refex Power Limited (subsidiary) was passed as an ordinary resolution, alongside a special resolution for making investments, giving loans, guarantees and providing security in excess of Section 186 limits [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.112].
- No loans or advances were provided to firms/companies in which directors were interested during FY2025-26, except loans extended to the subsidiary and wholly-owned subsidiaries [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.127].
- Cumulative related-party balances at 31 March 2026/2025 listed include trade receivables (e.g., from Sparzana Aviation Private Limited, Refex Airports and Transportation Private Limited, 3I Medical Equipment Technologies Private Limited, Refex Life Sciences Private Limited, Refex Holding Private Limited) and rental deposits payable [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.343].
- No material significant related party transaction in conflict with the Company's interest; disclosures in Note No. 40 [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.121].

## Inox Wind — related-party loan, guarantee, sales and receivable balances
- FY2025-26 vs FY2024-25: sales to related parties 12.88% vs 26% of total sales; loans & advances given to related parties 64.74% vs 44% of total loans & advances; investments in related parties 0% vs 0% of total investments [Inox Wind_Annual Report FY 2026 p.153].
- Loans to related parties include inter-corporate deposits with I-FOX Renewables & Infra Private Limited, IGREL Renewables Limited, Inox Neo Energies Private Limited and a performance guarantee in respect of Inox Neo Energies Private Limited [Inox Wind_Annual Report FY 2026 p.342].
- Standalone Annexure-A: aggregate loans/advances in the nature of loans repayable on demand to all parties = 2,11,663.40 lakh, all of which is to related parties; no terms/period of repayment specified; no overdue amount outstanding for more than ninety days [Inox Wind_Annual Report FY 2026 p.187].
- The Company may avail financial assistance from group entity Inox Clean Energy Limited and Promoter Director Shri Devansh Jain to meet fund requirements [Inox Wind_Annual Report FY 2026 p.68]; ICDs from ICEL are proposed as an efficient funding source with terms on arm's length basis [Inox Wind_Annual Report FY 2026 p.88], and loans from Shri Devansh Jain are proposed on arm's length terms [Inox Wind_Annual Report FY 2026 p.90].
- Proposed related party transaction limits of ₹1,750 Crore (39.80% of prior-year consolidated turnover; 622.75% of the related party's consolidated turnover) and ₹4,400 Crore (100.06% of prior-year consolidated turnover; 758.08% of the related party's consolidated turnover) both flagged as material RPTs [Inox Wind_Annual Report FY 2026 p.71][Inox Wind_Annual Report FY 2026 p.78].
- No guarantees were received or provided for any related party receivables or payables; expense recognised for doubtful ICD in respect of related-party amounts was NIL in FY2025-26 (₹1,346 lakh in FY2024-25) [Inox Wind_Annual Report FY 2026 p.238].
- Trade receivables: amounts due from customers representing >5% of total trade receivable were ₹2,83,306.55 lakh standalone as at 31 March 2026 (₹2,05,252.01 lakh as at 31 March 2025) from 5 major customers [Inox Wind_Annual Report FY 2026 p.241]; consolidated ₹2,71,477.09 lakh (₹1,93,600.71 lakh) from 5 major customers [Inox Wind_Annual Report FY 2026 p.322].
- Related-party transactions with IGESL and its subsidiaries include purchase/sale of goods and services, ICDs given/received, reimbursement of expenses [Inox Wind_Annual Report FY 2026 p.70][Inox Wind_Annual Report FY 2026 p.77]; ICEL group transactions are justified as providing operational and funding flexibility [Inox Wind_Annual Report FY 2026 p.88][Inox Wind_Annual Report FY 2026 p.69].
- No transactions with related parties in FY2025-26 in conflict with the Company's interest; disclosures in Note No. 38 standalone [Inox Wind_Annual Report FY 2026 p.134].

## Metal Coatings — FY2025 and FY2026 related-party exposures
- FY2026: all RPTs at arm's length and in ordinary course; material RPTs approved by shareholders; details in Note No. 34 [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.14]; no contracts/transactions not at arm's length for the year ended 31 March 2026 and no advances paid for related party transactions [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.31]; proposed transactions with a related party do not involve any loans, inter-corporate deposits, advances or investments [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2026 p.140].
- FY2025: no contracts/transactions not at arm's length for the year ended 31 March 2025; no advances paid for related party transactions [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2025 p.29]; all RPTs in ordinary course and at arm's length [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2025 p.11]; MRPTs entered into with Khandelwal Busar Industries Private Limited [Metal Coatings_Annual Report FY 2025 p.11].

Credit risk arising from trade receivables is managed in accordance with the Company’s established policy, procedures and control relating to customer credit risk management. The Company supplies wind turbine equipments to customers which are installed and commissioned generally by a group company and it involves various activities such as civil work, electrical & mechanical work and commissioning activities. The payment terms with customers are fixed as per industry norms. The above activities lead to certain amounts becoming due for payment on completion of related activities and commissioning. The Company considers such amounts as due only on completion of related milestones. However, the group company has also long term operation and maintenance contract with such customers. Details of the Related Party Transactions are disclosed in Note No. 34 to the Financial Statements forming part of this Annual Report. In terms of Regulation 23 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, transactions exceeding the materiality thresholds prescribed thereunder are considered Material Related Party Transactions (“MRPTs”) and require prior approval of the shareholders of the Company, irrespective of whether such transactions are undertaken in the ordinary course of business and on an arm’s length basis. Prior omnibus approval is obtained for related party transactions that are repetitive in nature and are entered into in the ordinary course of business and on an arm's length basis. All material related party transactions and their material modifications, if any, were entered into after being approved by the Company’s shareholders. The particulars of contracts and arrangements with related parties as required under Section 188(1) of the Act are provided in Form AOC-2, which forms part of this Report as Annexure II.

Further, the Company obtained the necessary prior omnibus approvals from the Audit Committee for related party transactions entered during the FY 2024–25. All contracts/arrangements/transactions entered into by the Company during the FY 2024-25 with related parties, as defined under the Act and SEBI Listing Regulations, were in the ordinary course of business and on arm’s length basis and were periodically placed before the Audit Committee of the Company for its review. The said limits are applicable, even if the transactions are in the ordinary course of business of the concerned company and at an arm’s length basis. chunks.section: Strong Promoter Support and Financial Backing
chunks.text: The Company continues to benefit from the strong backing of the INOXGFL Group, a well-established industrial group with a diversified presence across sectors. Promoter support has enabled improved financial flexibility and access to growth capital. The Group’s established industry presence and execution track record continue to reinforce stakeholder confidence. The Company has also seen continued participation from institutional investors, including both domestic and foreign investors. A balanced investor base supports long-term capital stability. Balance sheet strengthening initiatives and capital infusion measures undertaken in recent periods have improved liquidity and financial flexibility. **Bottom line:** Gammon India shows the most severe stress—going-concern doubts, fully eroded net worth, qualified audit opinions, and a pending resolution plan—while Refex faces quantified GST penalties and tax appeals, and Infosys has large tax contingencies and a US DOJ investigation but a very strong balance sheet. Materiality differs sharply: Gammon's legal/regulatory issues are existential relative to its financials, Refex's are moderate relative to its disclosures, and Infosys's are small relative to its scale, though the DOJ matter's outcome is unpredictable.

## Refex Industries legal/tax/regulatory proceedings and contingencies disclosure
- Refex discloses that it is involved in legal proceedings pending at varying levels of adjudication, including criminal proceedings, tax proceedings, statutory and regulatory actions, and other material pending litigation [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.320][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.238].
- GST assessment orders allege wrongful availment and utilisation of Input Tax Credit; penalties total ₹9,98,64,079, with appeals pending before the Commissioner of Central Tax (Appeals), Mysore (₹4,46,39,502), Commissioner (Appeal) of Customs & Indirect Taxes, Raipur (₹5,03,45,709 and ₹31,90,002), and Additional Commissioner, Jodhpur (₹16,88,866) [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.144].
- A state police penalty of ₹11,86,708 for traffic rule violation is disclosed [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.144].
- Refex has filed an appeal (IA (IBC)/1263/2025) before the NCLT against rejection of its claim arising from the liquidation of Landmark Housing Projects Chennai Private Limited, with hearing on 01.04.2026 reserved for orders [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.323].
- The Company has filed applications seeking withdrawal of certain statements made before the Registrar of Companies and other consequential reliefs, pending before the Madras High Court [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.323].
- An appeal is pending before the Commissioner of Income Tax Appeals, Chennai, against an order under Section 143(3) r.w.s. 147 of the Income Tax Act 1961 relating to long-term capital gains on sale of land and excess depreciation for FY2013-14, with tax demand of ₹821.13 Lakhs for AY2014-15 [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.323].
- The auditor identified assessment of contingent liabilities for direct/indirect tax litigations and third-party claims as a Key Audit Matter, with unexpected adverse outcomes disclosed in Note 34 [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.184]; the Group equivalent cites Note 38 [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.267].
- Refex's accounting policy states that show cause notices are not considered contingent liabilities unless converted into a demand [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.211][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.292].

## Refex Industries financial position to gauge materiality
- The evidence does not provide Refex's revenue, net profit, net worth or total assets in the cited chunks, so a precise ratio comparison cannot be made.
- Refex's consolidated financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2026 received an unmodified opinion [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.264]; standalone statements were also given a true and fair view [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.181].
- Ratio disclosures note an increase in net profit ratio due to higher revenue in a higher-margin segment, and a decline in current ratio on account of increased current liabilities [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.259].
- Refex declared a 1st interim dividend of ₹0.50 per share (25% of face value of ₹2), total outflow ₹646.40 Lakhs, and recommended a final dividend of ₹1 per share (50%) subject to AGM approval [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.296][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.215].

## Gammon India legal/tax/regulatory actions and contingent liabilities
- Gammon's auditor issued a qualified opinion on the standalone financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2026, except for the matter described in the Basis of Qualified Opinion paragraph [Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.67]; a qualified opinion was also issued on the consolidated financial statements [Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.142].
- Contingent liabilities disclosed include corporate/counter guarantees, disputed sales tax, service tax, income tax matters of the Company and joint ventures, disputed GST (₹0.22 crore paid under protest), disputed stamp duty, disputed provident fund (₹3.73 crore paid under protest), and right to recompense in favour of CDR lenders [Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.126][Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.203].
- A disputed UCO Bank demand pending since 1986 of USD 436,251 (₹3.02 crore) is disclosed, against which UCO Bank unilaterally adjusted a fixed deposit of USD 30,584 (₹0.21 crore) not accepted by the Company [Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.126][Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.203].
- Penal interest and excess interest charged by lenders amounted to ₹911.54 crore not accounted by the Holding Company as at March 31, 2026 [Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.203].
- The auditor noted delays in filing e-forms with the Registrar of Companies during FY2025-26 as mandated under the Companies Act, 2013 [Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.63].
- Remuneration paid to one executive director was not in accordance with Section 197 of the Act in the absence of an NOC from the consortium of lenders [Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.146].
- Carrying value of assets at certain terminated sites where access is restrained and the matter is under dispute is ₹0.95 crore [Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.72].
- Counterclaims in arbitration matters are described as liability unascertainable [Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.126][Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.203].

## Gammon India financial position and stress indicators for materiality assessment
- Auditors of overseas SPVs (Gammon Holdings B.V., Gammon International B.V., Pvan EERD Beheersmaatschappij B.V., ATSL Holdings B.V., Gammon Holding Mauritius Limited) carried material uncertainty related to going concern arising from current liabilities in excess of current assets and substantial erosion of net worth; the parent's resolution plan including dues to overseas SPVs is pending lender approval and lenders cannot reach consensus [Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.143].
- Gammon Holding BV: current liabilities exceed current assets by Euro 8.87 crore (₹966.77 crore) and net worth is fully eroded [Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.205].
- Gammon International BV: current liabilities exceed current assets by Euro 9.89 crore (₹1,078.10 crore) [Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.205].
- ATSL Holding BV: current liabilities exceed current assets by Euro 2.89 crore (₹315.46 crore) and net worth is fully eroded [Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.205].
- PvanEerd Beheersmaatschappij B.V.: current liabilities exceed current assets by Euro 2.50 crore (₹272.85 crore) [Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.205].
- Ansaldo Caldaie Boilers India Pvt Ltd: current liabilities exceed current assets by ₹54.81 crore, net worth eroded, and RBI directed refund of excess share application money; investment in Ansaldo GB-Engineering Pvt Ltd faces impairment and lenders took possession of properties for auction [Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.204].
- Standalone total equity was negative ₹11,755.05 crore as at March 31, 2026 versus negative ₹10,565.84 crore at March 31, 2025 [Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.81].
- Consolidated total equity was negative ₹13,212.55 crore as at March 31, 2026 [Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.151].
- Standalone loss before tax was ₹1,188.60 crore for FY2025-26 versus ₹1,109.64 crore in FY2024-25 [Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.82]; consolidated loss before tax was ₹1,159.24 crore versus ₹1,223.69 crore [Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.152].
- The Company is in default and not servicing its debt and interest obligations, and the debt service coverage ratio is therefore not given [Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.139].
- The auditor's report expresses a modified opinion on the adequacy and operating effectiveness of the Holding Company's internal financial controls with reference to consolidated financial statements [Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.146].

## Infosys regulatory, tax and legal matters including US/India proceedings
- The US Department of Justice is conducting an investigation into how the Company classified certain H-1B visa-recipient employees working for one client in immigration documents filed with US government authorities; the Company is in discussions with the DOJ and is unable to predict the outcome [infosys-ar-26 p.345].
- McCamish agreed to pay $17.5 million (approximately ₹150 crore) to settle class action lawsuits, with final court approval on December 18, 2025; the settlement has been paid and resolved all allegations without admission of liability, though McCamish may incur additional indeterminable costs from indemnities or damages [infosys-ar-26 p.345].
- Contingent liabilities: claims against the Company not acknowledged as debts, with amounts paid to statutory authorities of ₹2,399 crore (prior year ₹3,815 crore); India income tax matters amounted to ₹1,326 crore and ₹1,290 crore as at March 31, 2026 and March 31, 2025 respectively, relating to disallowance of software expenditure as capital and withholding tax on payments to Associated Enterprises, pending before various Income Tax Authorities [infosys-ar-26 p.262].
- On a consolidated basis, claims against the Group not acknowledged as debts included income tax matters of ₹1,964 crore and ₹1,933 crore as at March 31, 2026 and March 31, 2025; amounts paid to statutory authorities against tax claims were ₹2,594 crore and ₹4,199 crore [infosys-ar-26 p.344].
- During fiscal 2026, orders under Sections 250 and 254 of the Income-Tax Act, 1961 for AY2013-14 and AY2017-18 to 2021-22 confirmed the Company's position, resulting in interest income (pre-tax) of ₹381 crore recognised, income tax provision of ₹869 crore reversed, and ₹86 crore reduced from contingent liabilities [infosys-ar-26 p.79].
- Investor share-related disputes are described as not material in nature [infosys-ar-26 p.122].
- Infosys notes evolving regulatory compliance risk (immigration, wages, tax, sanctions) that could result in investigations, regulatory inquiries, litigation and fines [infosys-ar-26 p.147][infosys-ar-26 p.135].

## Infosys financial scale and provisions to compare materiality
- Consolidated revenue from operations was ₹1,78,650 crore for FY2025-26 versus ₹1,62,990 crore in FY2024-25 [infosys-ar-26 p.287][infosys-ar-26 p.33].
- Consolidated profit after tax was ₹29,440 crore, up from ₹26,713 crore [infosys-ar-26 p.81]; standalone PAT was ₹29,211 crore versus ₹25,568 crore [infosys-ar-26 p.81].
- Consolidated total assets were ₹1,55,967 crore as at March 31, 2026 [infosys-ar-26 p.286].
- Infosys has no outstanding borrowings; consolidated working capital was ₹51,167 crore including cash and cash equivalents of ₹22,201 crore and current investments of ₹12,950 crore [infosys-ar-26 p.319][infosys-ar-26 p.80].
- Consolidated cash and investments were ₹43,075 crore [infosys-ar-26 p.80].
- Return on net worth was 34.7% standalone and 30.3% consolidated [infosys-ar-26 p.81][infosys-ar-26 p.274], with current ratio 2.0 [infosys-ar-26 p.274].
- Consolidated income tax expense line shows deferred tax of ₹(1,246) crore and ₹(1,272) crore in the two years [infosys-ar-26 p.287] and there is an exceptional item for the impact of Labour Codes [infosys-ar-26 p.287][infosys-ar-26 p.356].

## Cross-company materiality comparison of legal/tax/regulatory exposures versus financials
- Gammon India: legal/regulatory and going-concern issues are existential—negative consolidated total equity of ₹13,212.55 crore [Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.151], default on debt servicing [Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.139], qualified audit opinions [Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.67][Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.142], and multiple overseas SPVs with fully eroded net worth and going-concern doubts [Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.143][Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.205]; unaccounted lender penal interest of ₹911.54 crore is large relative to the standalone loss before tax of ₹1,188.60 crore [Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.203][Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Gammon India Limited p.82].
- Refex Industries: GST penalties of ₹9,98,64,079 and an income tax demand of ₹821.13 Lakhs are quantified [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.144][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.323], but the evidence does not give Refex's revenue or net worth in the cited chunks, so a precise materiality ratio cannot be computed; its audit opinions are unmodified [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.264][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.181] and it continues to pay dividends [Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.296][Refex Industries_Annual Report FY 202526 p.215].
- Infosys: tax contingencies of ₹1,326 crore (standalone) and ₹1,964 crore (consolidated) [infosys-ar-26 p.262][infosys-ar-26 p.344] and the McCamish settlement of approximately ₹150 crore [infosys-ar-26 p.345] are small relative to consolidated revenue of ₹1,78,650 crore and PAT of ₹29,440 crore [infosys-ar-26 p.287][infosys-ar-26 p.81]; the DOJ H-1B investigation outcome is unpredictable [infosys-ar-26 p.345].
- The evidence does not state Refex's revenue, profit or net worth figures, so the Refex materiality comparison is only qualitative relative to its disclosed penalties and dividend capacity.

The contract conveys the right to control the use of an identified asset, if it involves the use of an identified asset and the Company has substantially all of the economic benefits from use of the asset and has the right to direct the use of the identified asset. The cost of the right-of-use asset shall comprise of the amount of the initial measurement of the lease liability adjusted for any lease payments made at or before the commencement date plus any initial direct costs incurred. chunks.text: i) Interest rate risk: A fall in the discount rate which is linked to the G.Sec. Rate will increase the present value of the liability requiring higher provision. A fall in the discount rate generally increases the mark to market value of the assets depending on the duration of asset. Salary Risk: The present value of the defined benefit plan liability is calculated by reference to the future salaries of members. As such, an increase in the salary of the members more than assumed level will increase the plan’s liability. Investment Risk: The present value of the defined benefit plan liability is calculated using a discount rate which is determined by reference to market yields at the end of the reporting period on government bonds. If the return on plan asset is below this rate, it will create a plan deficit. Currently, for the plan in India, it has a relatively balanced mix of investments in government securities, and other debt instruments. As a result interest income (pre-tax) of `327 crore was recognised and provision for income tax aggregating `183 crore was reversed with a corresponding credit to the Statement of Profit and Loss. In India, the Company has benefited from certain income tax incentives that the Government of India had provided for export of software and services from the units registered under the Special Economic Zones Act (SEZs), 2005 in the prior years. SEZ units which began the provision of services on or after April 1, 2005, are eligible for a deduction of 100% of profits or gains derived from the export of services for the first five years from the financial year in which the unit commenced the provision of services and 50% of such profits or gains for further five years. Up to 50% of such profits or gains is also available for a further five years subject to creation of a Special Economic Zone Re- investment reserve out of the profit for the eligible SEZ units and utilization of such reserve by the Company for acquiring new plant and machinery for the purpose of its business as per the provisions of the Income Tax Act, 1961. chunks.text: The measurement of financial liabilities depends on their classification, as described below: Financial liabilities at fair value through profit or loss include financial liabilities held for trading and financial liabilities designated upon initial recognition as at fair value through profit or loss. This category also includes derivative financial instruments entered into by the Company that are not designated as hedging instruments in hedge relationships as defined by Ind AS 109.Separated embedded derivatives are also classified as held for trading unless they are designated as effective hedging instruments. Gains or losses on liabilities held for trading are recognized in the statement of profit and loss. Financial liabilities designated upon initial recognition at fair value through profit or loss are designated at the initial date of recognition, and only if the criteria in Ind AS 109 are satisfied.

Investment Risk: The present value of the defined benefit plan liability is calculated using a discount rate which is determined by reference to market yields at the end of the reporting period on government bonds. Mortality risk: Since the benefits under the plan is not payable for life time and payable till retirement age only, plan does not have any longevity risk. Currently, for the plan in India, it has a relatively balanced mix of investments in government securities, and other debt instruments. d) Asset Liability Matching Risk: The plan faces the ALM risk as to the matching cash flow. Since the plan is invested in lines of Rule 101 of Income Tax Rules, 1962, this generally reduces ALM risk. e) Mortality risk: Since the benefits under the plan is not payable for life time and payable till retirement age only, plan does not have any longevity risk. f) Concentration Risk: Plan is having a concentration risk as all the assets are invested with the insurance company and a default will wipe out all the assets. Although probability of this is very less as insurance companies have to follow regulatory guidelines.

During the quarter ended March 31, 2025, the Company received orders under section 250 of the Income Tax Act, 1961, from the Income Tax Authorities in India for the assessment years, 2016-17 and 2019-20. These orders confirmed the Company's position with respect to tax treatment of certain matters. As a result interest income (pre-tax) of `327 crore was recognised and provision for income tax aggregating `183 crore was reversed with a corresponding credit to the Statement of Profit and Loss. Also, upon resolution of the disputes, an amount aggregating to `1,068 crore has been reduced from contingent liabilities. The foreign tax expense is due to income taxes payable overseas, principally in the United States. In India, the Company has benefited from certain income tax incentives that the Government of India had provided for export of software and services from the units registered under the Special Economic Zones Act (SEZs), 2005 in the prior years. SEZ units which began the provision of services on or after April 1, 2005, are eligible for a deduction of 100% of profits or gains derived from the export of services for the first five years from the financial year in which the unit commenced the provision of services and 50% of such profits or gains for further five years. Up to 50% of such profits or gains is also available for a further five years subject to creation of a Special Economic Zone Re- investment reserve out of the profit for the eligible SEZ units and utilization of such reserve by the Company for acquiring new plant and machinery for the purpose of its business as per the provisions of the Income Tax Act, 1961.
